in_sanskrit.name: अनुग्रह
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: अनुग्रहः (Anugrahah) is a Sanskrit word that refers to divine grace, compassion, and mercy. It is derived from the root word 'anu' (towards) and 'grah' (grasps), meaning 'to grasp towards'. In Hinduism, Anugrah is often depicted as a divine power that showers blessings upon devotees. It is also the name of several Hindu gods and goddesses, including Ganesha, Durga, and Vishnu, who are believed to bestow grace and mercy upon their devotees.

in_hindi.name: अनुग्रह
in_hindi.long_meaning: अनुग्रह (Anugrah) हिंदी में 'प्रसाद' (prasad - grace), 'प्रसन्नता' (prasanna-tā - happiness), और 'आशा' (āśā - hope) के साथ-साथ संबद्ध है।

in_tamil.name: அனுக்ரவா
in_tamil.long_meaning: அனுக்ரவா (Anukravā) அடிகலம் தமிழ் மொழியில் 'விளக்கம்' (vilakkam - guidance), 'அழையவும்' (azhaiyavum - comforting), और 'அரியம்' (ariyam - benevolence) கூழல்களில் உள்ளது.

in_telugu.name: అనుగ్రాధ
in_telugu.long_meaning: అనుగ్రాధ (Anugrādh) తెలుగు మொழிయిల్లేదూ 'ప్రదేశ' (pradēśa - control), 'ప్రసాద' (prasāda - grace), అథయే 'మృదుచెద్ద' (mṛduchedda - tender) సందేశముదూ.
